3.text: carries a small twig of willow, around which he winds a piece of thread

4.text: received from one of the old women. Then he removes the thread, and

5.text: winds it around his right wrist, but neither ties nor fastens it. The twig is

6.text: put on the hearth as a purifying sacrifice, destroying any unclean influence

7.text: caused by contact with the dead body. The thread wound around the wrist

8.text: is worn there till it drops off, which will happen after a day or two.

9.text: All the members of the procession, holding one another by the hand,

10.text: form a large ring, which is encircled by that part of the thong that was

11.text: taken home from the funeral. Each of the members takes hold of it, and

12.text: each one cuts off the part nearest to himself. This severs all connection

13.text: between them; and the spirit of the deceased, if it should ever come back,

14.text: would have to find them out one by one. The pieces of the thong are gener-

15.text: ally wound around the waist for a belt, though any other use is also admissible.
